summary: Pacing and motion night: our Shorts change shot size about every 2 seconds and place every beat, while the reference Shorts hold one move per 4-6 s shot, so I added the numbers to the owner's calm-camera test. Added one topic: NVIDIA's first chip, a 1.78M-view breakout.
why: In each of our last five Shorts, every ~6 s beat has 3 camera keys and 3 shot sizes, against 46% static and 33% push-in shots of 4-6 s in 13 reference Shorts. Crossrail, the one-machine Short, kept 0.73 of its post-hook viewers to the end, against 0.11-0.32 for the others. True Campside Stories' NVIDIA's First Chip has 1.78M views on 29.8K subscribers (60x).

findings.title: We cut the camera about three times as often as the reference Shorts
findings.detail: Ours: 3 shot sizes in every 6 s beat and a new place every beat. Branch Education, Professor Of AI and Inside Decoded: one move or none in a 4-6 s shot. Added to the tech-calm-camera challenger.

findings.title: The one-machine Short keeps people to the end
findings.detail: Crossrail end hold 0.73, against microwave 0.11, dam 0.15 and transistor 0.32. Added to tech-one-machine-one-place.

findings.title: NVIDIA's First Chip: 1.78M views on 29.8K subscribers
findings.detail: A chip-history breakout, added as an invention_story topic with JPR and SiliconANGLE figures (NV1 about 250 thousand transistors, Rubin 336 billion).

findings.title: Microsoft 365 outage: figures yes, demand no
findings.detail: The preliminary report gives the causes, but there is no 100K+ explainer this week, so there is no long video for it.

findings.title: Claude Code 2.1.331
findings.detail: Cloud turns and subagents retry once instead of failing when a reply goes silent mid-thinking. That should mean fewer failed routine runs, with nothing to change.
